mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during the same month, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in the month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such labor conditions are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) or unemployment does not fall below 4% while payroll gains persist.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) exceeding 5% year-over-year coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), indicating a shift from supply-side to demand-side growth, which is associated with higher S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY > +5% AND INDPRO < previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05) or the demand surge is not accompanied by a production decline.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.5 suggests supply-side weakness, which reduces market capacity and elevates S&P 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate profit expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) or INDPRO recovers in the following month without further declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 233.0 indicates deflationary pressure, lowering real discount rates and pushing S&P 20-day forward returns higher.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day moving average during the deflationary period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a strong labor market signal that, when sustained for 1 month, is associated with negative S&P 60-day forward returns due to overvalued equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the low-unemployment period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both retail (HOUST) and industrial demand (RSAFS) above 400K and 420K respectively for two consecutive months indicates robust overall demand, which predicts positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 400K AND RSAFS > 420K for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) or either demand series fails to meet thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 99.5 for three consecutive months signals supply-side expansion, which, if persistent, is expected to lower S&P 60-day forward returns as market expectations adjust to higher supply.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average during the expansion period.
